bc_kid_s_cliff.blurb: A small sport crag in the Northern Crags section of Skaha Bluffs, close to Okanagan Falls. It holds 18 bolted lines of about 20 metres, with an even spread from 5.9 up to the low 5.12s: plenty of 5.9 to 5.11 for a mid-grade day, and a handful of harder ones. The stone is mostly polished slab with weathered holds, so the moves feel more delicate than the grade suggests; the steeper sections are the exception, and the harder lines are thin and technical. The face looks east, so it gets the morning sun and is out of it by afternoon, with trees at the base giving extra shade. It sits well off the busiest Skaha walls, which keeps it quieter.

bc_open_book_wall.blurb: A tall, west-looking wall on Kinnaird Bluffs at the south edge of Castlegar, in the West Kootenays, and the nearest cliff to the roadside start of the trail. It carries 18 routes, a fairly even mix of sport (10) and trad (8), most with a pitch or two. Grades start around 5.7 and run to the low 5.12s, but the bulk sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a few easier trad lines for those building up. The wall is known for its crack and corner climbing alongside steeper bolted faces. Being the closest wall to the car makes it a handy first stop, and the base is walled in so voices carry to the neighbours below.
bc_open_book_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the pull-out on Sahlstrom Road, a short way up from where it leaves 37th Street in south Castlegar. The trail to the wall starts close by and is only about 100 m.

bc_woodstock.blurb: Woodstock is a mostly sport crag within Murrin Park, on the Sea to Sky highway just south of Squamish. Of its 18 routes, 15 are bolted, with two trad lines and a single boulder problem. Grades run from about 5.7 up through the 5.12s and 5.13s to a lone 5.14, with a good cluster of 5.9 and 5.11 climbs. It is popular with newer leaders and club trips because the lines are steep without being unfriendly, and the easier ones make good warm-ups. It is one of many crags linked by the park's loop trail, so it is easy to combine with neighbouring cliffs, and a lake nearby is a favourite place to cool off after the day.

bc_bulletheads_central.blurb: The central section of the Bulletheads, a run of tall rounded buttresses on the Stawamus Chief above Squamish. Climbs here are long multi-pitch lines, mostly four or five pitches, that start from the trail along the base and finish on the summits of the tallest bullets. Of the 18 routes, 15 are trad and 3 are sport. It is a serious step up in commitment from the smaller, ledge-linked sections to the south. Grades run from 5.9 to 5.13, but nearly all fall at 5.10 and 5.11, with ten at 5.11 alone, so this suits confident leaders who are comfortable with a full day on the wall.
